solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sweeping changes finally cutting tax

indicators.note: a letter cutting into a word sits inside it, so the tax word is opened up here

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word changes

explanation.surface: A government's sweeping changes end up cutting a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes S, the last letter of 'changes', and 'cutting' puts it inside VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sweeping is broad and enormous in extent.

clue.text: Stumped by prevalent conflict

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
rife means widespread or prevalent

explanation.surface: A cricketer is stumped amid widespread disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'stumped' when the wicketkeeper breaks the stumps while he is out of his ground; scorecards abbreviate it ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: strife is bitter conflict or discord.

clue.text: Introduction to blessing of Pope holding ring, I rub tribe the wrong way

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the ring letter inside them
rubbing a tribe the wrong way rearranges the letters of the preceding words

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clumsy cleric irritates a tribe while the Pope holds his ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' rearranges I RUB TRIBE to URBIETRBI, and 'holding' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase meaning 'to the city and the world' opens the Pope's solemn Easter and Christmas benediction.

clue.text: Raid botched over American range of operation

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits over the second
a botched job is messed up, so the letters of raid are scrambled

parts.note: US is short for United States, i.e. American

explanation.surface: A bungled raid over American territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges RAID to RADI, and 'over' places it above US in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a radius is the distance within which something can operate.

clue.text: Airs bound to get Great Britain in extremely secluded place

parts.note: so can mean very or extremely, as in so tired

indicators.note: the country letters go inside the hideaway word

parts.note: a nook is a sheltered corner

explanation.surface: Tunes are destined to reach Britain in a remote hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs bound' means tunes bound together in a volume; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound volume of songs collects many tunes, here called airs, between covers.

clue.text: Region shortly to welcome Israelites, primarily?

definitions.text: Region shortly to welcome Israelites, primarily?

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so a letter goes inside
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a zone is a region or area

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of Israelites

explanation.surface: A promised land is soon to receive the people of Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ZONE to ZON and 'to welcome' puts I (first of Israelites, from 'primarily') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical homeland promised to the Israelites, a region awaiting their arrival.

clue.text: Aquatic hunter with angle to sell

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod
to hawk is to peddle goods

explanation.surface: A fishmonger catches fish with a rod and then peddles them.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey, a raptor that hunts fish by plunging into water, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Computer list comes up with device editor not working

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a menu is a list of options on a computer screen
a ploy is a stratagem or device

explanation.surface: A computer menu pops up, but the device and its editor are broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns MENU into UNEM in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone jobless is out of work, without employment.

clue.text: It's not so sensible losing head in pursuit

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: dafter means sillier, less sensible

explanation.surface: Someone becomes less sensible, losing their head in a chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the D from DAFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go after someone is to chase them, so in pursuit.

clue.text: A blessing, including "enlightened" one in emancipation

indicators.note: the blessing word includes the next letters within it

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
lit means lighted up, enlightened
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An enlightened blessing was part of the freeing of slaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' is the container signal; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ending of slavery was called its abolition, the emancipation of slaves.

clue.text: City I built is unfortunately lacking university

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is a mess, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means a letter must be taken from the pool

explanation.surface: A builder laments that the city he built has no university.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U from the letters of I BUILT IS, then 'unfortunately' rearranges the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Georgia in the Caucasus is a city.

clue.text: Skirt potential live performance involving northern radio fan

indicators.note: involving means taking the letter in

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A northern radio enthusiast at a gig chases a potential girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts N inside GIG. 'Skirt potential' means material that could become a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked cotton cloth is a fabric that might be made into a skirt.

clue.text: Wife in Australian spring-cleaning time cleaned with a broom

indicators.note: the wife letter goes inside the month

parts.note: September falls in spring in the southern hemisphere, abbreviated SEPT

explanation.surface: A wife in Australia does her spring cleaning with a broom.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring in Australia falls in September, so spring-cleaning time there is SEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of sweep, which is cleaning a floor with brush or broom.

clue.text: Female artist's anxiety about line in cup

indicators.note: the anxiety word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: stress is anxiety or strain

indicators.note: the line letter goes into the cup

parts.note: taken as the word cup

explanation.surface: A woman artist worries about a line on a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'about' are two nested containers, giving CULP inside the split anxiety word. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who carves or models statues is a female sculptor, an artist.

clue.text: Deficiency in whisky, perhaps a drop

parts.note: a short is a spirit drink such as whisky, perhaps signalling an example
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A deficiency in the whisky, perhaps just a drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shortfall is an amount by which something falls short, a deficit.

clue.text: Smack in tale involved barely touching

parts.note: a smack is a taste or flavour, a tang

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A slap features in a tale that's barely relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a blow; here it is a flavour. 'involved' rearranges IN TALE to ENTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent line meets a curve at a single point, so it only just touches it.

clue.text: Imprisoned doctor drunkenly had coke but not heroin

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered
but not means a letter is excluded from the pool

parts.note: H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drunken doctor took cocaine but stopped short of heroin, and was jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram verb: remove H from DRUNKENLY HAD COKE and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: kept securely locked away, as a prisoner is.

clue.text: Deity unexpectedly taking chap heavenward in blast

indicators.note: taking in means holding the reversed piece inside
unexpectedly means the letters of deity turn up in a new order
in a down entry going heavenward is reading upwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A god unexpectedly whisks a man up to heaven in an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' gives DYITE and 'heavenward' gives NAM, which 'taking' holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive is used for blasting, so stands for a blast.

clue.text: Recovered from party, the object being to binge

parts.note: being over an illness means having recovered from it
a do is a party
it is the pronoun used for an object

explanation.surface: Having recovered from a party, the aim is to go on another bender.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go too far or overindulge, as a binge does.

clue.text: European notes among loads of money? Son's having none of it

indicators.note: among puts the next letters within the money words

parts.note: piles means a great deal of money
n is a dictionary abbreviation for note, so two notes give NN
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Euro notes amid piles of cash, but the son has none of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal. The definition 'having none of it' refers back to 'money' earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: With no cash at all, a person is broke, possessing none of the money.

clue.text: Lord embracing holy woman or vice versa?

definitions.text: Lord embracing holy woman or vice versa?

indicators.note: embracing means holding the saint letters inside

parts.note: Sir is the title for a knight or lord
Ste is the abbreviation for a female saint

explanation.surface: A lord embraces a nun, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' is the container. The vice versa reading is a nun embracing the Lord in devotion, which defines the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a holy woman devoted to God, so embraced by the Lord and embracing Him.

clue.text: Editor accepts honour to attach journalist to military unit

definitions.text: to attach journalist to military unit

indicators.note: accepts means taking the honour inside

parts.note: MBE is the British honour Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An editor accepts an honour for sending a reporter with the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: War reporters assigned to travel with troops are said to be embedded with a unit.

clue.text: Bit parts as outlaw?

parts.note: the word bit split into its parts reads as ..., a brigand

explanation.surface: An actor playing small roles as a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit parts' looks like minor acting roles; split BIT into its parts and you have B and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber living outside the law is an outlaw, a brigand.

clue.text: Wrinkly bottom was best

parts.note: the rump is the backside, bottom
led means was in front, was best

explanation.surface: A wrinkly backside was judged the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: creased or crumpled clothes or sheets are wrinkly.

clue.text: Time to give up?

parts.note: reads as a time to quit, but means the Christian season when people forgo luxuries

explanation.surface: Is it time to throw in the towel?
explanation.definitionFit: The forty days before Easter are traditionally spent abstaining from some pleasure.

clue.text: Evil customers at a nice show

indicators.note: show means these words show, reveal, the letters within them

explanation.surface: Customers at a nice show turn out to be wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a performance; it reveals the letters in customerS AT A NICe.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish, of the Devil, is what wicked or evil can mean.

clue.text: Clubs request a lot of beer, perhaps

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Clubs order a large amount of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel holds a great deal of liquid, beer being one example.

clue.text: Start burning unless turned over in dried up surroundings

indicators.note: in places the reversed word within the dry word
the dry word forms the surroundings of the middle

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered

indicators.note: turned over means the word for unless is read backwards

parts.note: if not means unless

explanation.surface: Unless turned over, the dry surroundings will catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes IF NOT into TONFI, placed in SERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to ignite something is to make it start burning.

clue.text: English novelist has to be objected to

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists
has shortens to 's

explanation.surface: An English novelist must face objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something wrong or faulty is objectionable, so open to objection.
